clinician.trajectory_summary: A 41-year-old female presented with a 5-month history of intermittent right anteromedial thigh pain and urinary frequency/urgency. Imaging workup (ultrasound, CT, MRI) identified a 44×42×28 mm mass on the right anterior bladder wall. Ultrasound showed a hypoechoic lesion; CT demonstrated a soft-tissue attenuation mass protruding into the bladder lumen with equivocal mild enhancement; MRI revealed a heterogeneous intramural (rather than intraluminal) mass. Cystoscopy visualized a large mass indenting the right bladder wall that was mobile on bimanual examination. Urine culture and cytology were negative for infection and malignancy. Surgical exploration revealed the mass was extramural and adjacent to the right inferolateral bladder wall. The lesion was circumferentially dissected free without requiring partial cystectomy, with uneventful post-operative recovery. Histopathology confirmed benign leiomyoma composed of interweaving bands of bland smooth muscle with no cell atypia.
